thread_a.role: io_uring file registration mutates table size (under lock)

emergent_bug.violated_requirement: rho = atomic([read(ctx->file_table.data.nr)]) from thread_b (the trace read must not race a concurrent registration write)
emergent_bug.violating_event: e@io_sqe_files_register:541 = write(ctx->file_table.data.nr) by a concurrent register syscall
emergent_bug.missing_guarantee: registration mutates nr while holding ctx->uring_lock, but in the vuln version the trace read at register.c:909 happens AFTER mutex_unlock(&ctx->uring_lock); the reader no longer holds the lock during the read, so no serialize(g) covers both sites and the atomicity the reader assumes is not established
emergent_bug.category_rationale: rho is atomic(single access) broken by a concurrent conflicting write while the reader is outside the lock -> data race

fix_maps_to: patch moves trace_io_uring_register to before mutex_unlock(&ctx->uring_lock) -> the read now executes under ctx->uring_lock, adding serialize(ctx->uring_lock, [read nr]) that shares the lock with the writer and establishes the atomic requirement
recall_risk_notes: Concrete missing-lock case the design targets: object and both sites are in the static surface, the fix is a real lock-scope extension, and detecting it needs only intra-function lock-scope reasoning (the read at line 909 is after mutex_unlock, so get_lock_protection should report it unprotected). Risks: (1) self-race / same-entry MHP - both contexts are concurrent invocations of the same io_uring_register syscall, so the design must admit a same-entry concurrent thread pair; (2) the race is benign (trace-only, author 'we don't care much'), so the LLM may adjudicate the read as not carrying a real order intent and reject it.
